pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Thallium Toxicity (Thallotoxicosis / Thallium Poisoning) THE SMOKING GUN: The classic clinical triad of acute gastrointestinal distress, followed by excruciatingly painful axonal peripheral neuropathy (hyperpathia/burning feet), and delayed rapid-onset alopecia with Mees' lines on the nails. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium ions share a similar ionic radius to potassium and readily displace potassium in biological processes by entering cells via Na+/K+-ATPase pumps. Once intracellular, thallium inhibits key enzymes in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle and oxidative phosphorylation (such as pyruvate kinase), disrupting cellular ATP production. Furthermore, thallium cross-links with sulfhydryl groups on structural proteins, leading to widespread axonal degeneration, cellular necrosis, and disruption of keratin synthesis, which culminates in rapid hair follicle loss and nail matrix dysfunction.
